reason: Measured, not read. Two independent methods (canvas font metrics; a zero-height inline-block anchored on the first line's baseline) agree on the true first-baseline deltas of .b-away against its own .b-title, identical on every row: phone/day 390 = +2.0px (finding claims +1), desk 768/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440 = -3.0px (finding claims -5), print sheet = +3.0px (only number it gets right). Two of three figures are wrong, and the one it stakes its argument on is overstated by 67%. Worse, desk is the surface where the setting is demonstrably CORRECT. At 1440 the figure is 17px Geist Mono (digit cap 12px) and the title 24px Geist 600 (cap 17px). At the shipped -3px the figure's ink band runs from title-baseline-15 to title-baseline-3, so its optical centre sits at -9.0 against the title's cap-band centre at -8.5: a 0.5px agreement. That is textbook optical setting of a small numeral against a much larger head - centred on the cap band, not hung off the baseline - and the crop confirms it: '16' stands level with 'Menu tasting at The Orchard'. The 'reads as a superscript' claim is false by construction; a superscript's ink sits at or above cap top, and this figure's ink straddles the title's x-height. The finding's own diagnosis defeats it: it treats 'their half-leadings can never agree at any size pairing' as the fault, when at 17-against-24 you do not WANT the baselines to agree. Forcing the proposed +/-0.5px baseline lock would drop the desk figure 3px and seat a 12px-cap numeral low against a 17px-cap title - the fix makes the flagship width worse, and desk is five of the seven measured widths. The premise is also mischaracterised: this is not 'one line of text'. The figure sits across a 110px (phone) / 124px (desk) gutter with the vertical rail and the indigo tick between it and the title. The L644 assertion it cites as the missing discipline governs .b-title/.b-date/.b-grabWord - three lines stacked inside one .b-copy, genuinely adjacent - which is a different alignment problem. Finally the fix cannot be applied as written and was not checked against the DOM: .b-away is a SIBLING of .b-copy inside .b-item (render-b.js row(), with a .b-vh.b-unitSaid span and .b-tick between them), not a child, so '.b-copy as a two-column grid with .b-away as the first cell' is impossible without moving the node and its screen-reader unit span in render-b.js. And folding an 84px column plus a 40px gap inside .b-copy, which carries max-width:544px, cuts the title measure from 544px to 420px and re-breaks every title that render-core.js word-safe-trims. Only print (+3.0px, 17px mono against 17px sans, where baselines are unambiguous) is arguably loose, and the finding does not isolate it - it asserts the opposite, that all three should be zero.
sharpenedFix: Nothing to do at desk or phone. If anything is worth a look it is the printed sheet in isolation, and the cause is not leading: b.css:1255 sets '.b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-body) }' (15px), but the >=701px block at b.css:1283 re-states '[data-medium="sheet"] .b-away { font-size: var(--size-lead) }' at equal specificity and later in source, so the sheet renders a 17px figure against a 17px title - the print intent was never re-declared inside the media query the way '.b-print .b-title' was. Restating '[data-medium="sheet"] .b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-body) }' would restore the intended 15/17 pairing; the residual baseline offset would then be a two-pixel top nudge on the print rule, not a grid rewrite. Leave .b-away absolutely positioned and leave the transform that carries it with .b-copy - the interaction-check |away.top - copy.top| < 4px assertion depends on it.
